title: Second incompleteness and Löb's theorem

based_on.title: An Introduction to Gödel's Theorems, second edition, corrected Logic Matters reprint

summary: Prove Löb's theorem and use the specified PA proof predicate to show why consistent PA cannot prove its own consistency sentence.
abstract: A proof that arithmetic never proves a contradiction would be a reassuring mathematical result. Could arithmetic itself supply that proof? For the precise consistency sentence attached to our proof checker, Gödel's second incompleteness theorem gives a negative answer if Peano arithmetic is consistent. We derive it from Löb's theorem: whenever the theory proves that the provability of a particular sentence would guarantee that sentence, it already proves the sentence. The argument makes the roles of self-reference and the three derivability conditions explicit. It also explains how a consistent extension of arithmetic can assert that the original theory has a proof of contradiction, despite there being no such ordinary finite proof.
